name: Private Eye Cyclops crossword No 641
preamble: Running clockwise around the shaded squares, starting top left, is an extract (slightly edited to fit the grid) from an instalment of our feature, ‘The Headmistress Writes’ (Mrs T. May) in 2018. The 52 letters of the quote not intersecting with clue answers are: AAAAA B C D EEE F G HHH IIIIII KKK LLL M NN OOOOO P RR SSSS TTT UUUU YY

solutions.check: 68 entries verified against the grid image (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping); unclued letters checked against the preamble's list

clue.text: Quit protecting Conservative’s back – cry

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it on all sides, so one word wraps round another
a word's back is its rear end, so only the final letter is wanted

blocks.note: scram means clear off, quit the scene
the final letter of Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory under siege howls as someone abandons the job of guarding their back.
explanation.walkthrough: Scram (clear off) holds the last letter of Conservative, giving SCREAM. 'Back' looks like part of the bodyguard picture but only picks one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a loud, piercing shout, so the verb works as a synonym for crying out.

clue.text: It stops you from playing bloody joker

blocks.note: blood is red, so bloody suggests the colour
a card is a comic, a joker

explanation.surface: Something keeps you away from playing with a bloody joker, perhaps a sulky card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody joker' reads as an insult, but it splits into a colour and an old word for a wag.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee shows a red card to send a footballer off, which ends their participation in the match.

clue.text: O, it could be Trump’s first introduction to darned exercise

indicators.note: first points to the initial letter of the word before it and nothing more
something introduced to a thing is put into it, so one piece is slipped inside

blocks.note: darned and bloody are both mild curses
the initial letter of Trump
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A gasp of 'O' greets the news that Trump is about to take up some wretched exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading 'O' reads as an exclamation, but it is the letter O, and the clue defines by example. Darned and bloody are both mild British curses.
explanation.definitionFit: Group O is one of the four main human blood groups in the ABO system, so it is an example.

clue.text: Toffee-nosed, prick-like son replaces Korean leader

the first letter of Korean

explanation.walkthrough: KNOBBY loses its leading K to S, giving SNOBBY. Toffee-nosed is British slang for stuck-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee-nosed is a British colloquialism for snooty, looking down on others, which is a close synonym.

clue.text: Poet that pissed in the boss’s position?

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: The boss holds the highest rank in an organisation, so occupying that place means being at the summit.

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The fool's letters are reworked round I to give FOLIO after PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister without portfolio holds cabinet rank but has no specific department, so a portfolio is exactly what such a minister lacks.

clue.text: DIY injury mutilated flesh on member

blocks.note: taken as written
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.walkthrough: DIY usually means home improvement; here it means injury done to oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-harm is deliberate injury inflicted on one's own body, and DIY means doing it yourself.

the opening letter of cock

clue.text: Easily distracted hacks should have these fitted

definitions.text: Easily distracted hacks should have these fitted

blocks.note: surface reading: journalists who lose focus
setter's reading: hacks are riding horses, and skittish ones wear eye shields

explanation.walkthrough: Hacks look like journalists, which fits Private Eye, but a hack is also a horse kept for ordinary riding.
explanation.definitionFit: Blinkers are leather flaps on a bridle that block a horse's side vision so it stays calm and focused.

clue.text: New don rearranged cleavage as preferred by some painters

indicators.note: rearranged plainly means put in a different order

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written
a rip is a split, a cleaving apart

explanation.surface: A new academic rearranges a woman's neckline the way certain artists like it.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleavage suggests a low neckline, but it means a split or tear. The painters are decorators, not artists.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-drip paint is a thick gloss that does not run, favoured by house decorators for tidy work.

clue.text: Be assertive and succeed in pressuring political enforcer

blocks.note: to crack a problem is to succeed in solving it
a party whip enforces voting discipline by leaning on MPs

explanation.surface: Advice for MPs: stand firm and get the better of the party's enforcer.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics the whip is the party official who keeps MPs voting the party line.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack the whip is to use authority firmly to make others work harder, an idiom for asserting control.

clue.text: Directly in front of party faction wanting a leader

blocks.note: the right wing of a political party
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: The party's right-wing faction is crying out for a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' looks like lacking, a removal signal, but it only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Right ahead means straight in front, so 'directly' matches right and 'in front' matches ahead.

clue.text: Just a few drops surprisingly loosen up fat

indicators.note: a surprising result is unexpected, so the letters come out in an unforeseen order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tip that a tiny amount of something will break down fat.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a cooking or diet tip; the last three words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaspoonful is a very small measure of liquid, only a few drops more or less.

clue.text: House no use on money problem that might come after marriage

indicators.note: no means without, so the following letters are removed
a problem is something to work out, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newlywed couple's house is useless; money troubles may follow the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No use' reads as worthless, but it tells you to strip USE from the word before.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeymoon is the holiday a couple takes immediately after their wedding, so it follows marriage.

clue.text: Tone of Scottish politician, endless prick

indicators.note: endless means without an end, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: Alex Salmond, former SNP leader and First Minister of Scotland
to pink is to pierce or prick with small holes

explanation.surface: A Scottish politician's tone gets him called an endless prick.
explanation.walkthrough: Tone suggests manner of speaking, but it is a shade of colour. 'Prick' is not the insult but a verb meaning pierce.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmon pink is a shade, the orange-pink of salmon flesh, and a tone is a shade of a colour.

clue.text: Bastard in haste, in brewing drink

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so these letters are stirred up

blocks.note: B is the polite abbreviation for bastard, as in 'the old b'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some rogue in a hurry knocks back a strong drink as it brews.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' places the single letter with the next words; the second 'in' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong anise-flavoured spirit, so it is one kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Glorified old flame (ring a bell? Ed.)

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
to toll is to ring a bell
Ed. is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A former lover is idealised; does that remind you of anyone, Editor?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring a bell' means sound familiar, but here it is literal. Ed. nods to Private Eye's editor, Ian Hislop.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, so the past tense matches glorified as praised.

clue.text: Character has look into misshapen penis

indicators.note: into means going inside, so one piece is put within
misshapen means deformed, so the letters are twisted out of shape

blocks.note: taken as written
lo means look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: A man inspects a deformed part of his anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: Character looks like a person, but it is a letter of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a character is a written letter or symbol.

clue.text: Standing US politician shortly to go against a Native American

indicators.note: shortly means in brief, so the word is cut down

blocks.note: a member of the US House of Representatives
the Ute are a Native American people of the Rockies

explanation.surface: An American politician on his feet is about to take on a Native American.
explanation.walkthrough: Standing looks like the politician upright, but it means reputation; the trimmed title is the familiar abbreviation Rep.
explanation.definitionFit: Repute is reputation, the regard in which one is held, which is what standing means here.

clue.text: Hello! categorically covers place

indicators.note: to cover something is to contain it, so the letters lie within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: Hello! magazine flatly reports where someone lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! is a British celebrity magazine, so the exclamation mark looks like a greeting but belongs to the title.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something can mean to identify where it is, the same as finding its position.

clue.text: New version of old lecher cuddling up Cyclops

indicators.note: to cuddle is to wrap one's arms round, so one piece embraces another
in a down entry, up means reading from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: a rake is a dissolute womaniser
Cyclops is the setter, so refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter, Cyclops, is cosied up to by an ageing letch in a fresh production.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for the first-person pronoun, a common convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A remake is a new version of an earlier film or song, made again with fresh treatment.

clue.text: Major financial concerns about a very obvious depression

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: the City is London's financial district
taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Big financial firms worry about a deep economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: Depression reads as an economic slump, matching the finance theme, but it is a physical hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity is a hollow space, a dip or hole, which is a depression in a surface.
